quote: However, Supply Agreement § 14.2 provides that any change in direct or indirect ownership of more than 50% of the Company's voting stock "shall be deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Customer and shall require the prior written consent of Supplier." The SPA transaction is a 100% change in ownership. ... The closing condition in § 7.2(c) is effectively inoperative. It requires that "all consents, approvals and notices set forth on Schedule 4.4" be received. Since Schedule 4.4 lists nothing, Buyer has no contractual right to refuse Closing even if Vantrell has not consented. ... If Closing occurs without Vantrell's consent, Vantrell may terminate the Supply Agreement on 30 days' notice (Supply Agreement § 14.2)
reason: The memo meets every element of the criterion. It identifies that Supply Agreement § 14.2 treats a change of more than 50% of voting stock as an assignment that needs Vantrell's prior written consent. It notes the 30-day termination right and states that the 100% stock sale triggers it. It explains that SPA § 4.4 and Schedule 4.4 ('None') fail to disclose the consent and that the § 7.2(c) closing condition does not cover it. It recommends adding the consent to the schedule and making it a closing condition.
